 (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023  COMMON JUDGMENT  The petitioners have filed these two claim petitions against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by them in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. Since these two cases are arising out of one and same accident and cause of action are the same and the respondents are the same and to avoid multiplicity of proceedings and to avoid outcome of conflicting Judgments, these two cases are clubbed together.
M.V.C.No.1764/2023 clubbed with original M.V.C.No.723/2023
and common evidence came to be recorded in the said case.
These two cases are proceeded for disposal by way of common Judgment.

03 . The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
 That on 09.01.2023 at about 07.30 p.m, wherein the petitioner in M.V.C.No.723/2023 being a rider and the petitioner in M.V.C.No.1764/2023 being the pillion rider was going from Sathnoor towards Doddalahalli side, on the extreme left side of Sathnoor - Doddalahalli Road, when they reached near Solar  (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 Plant, Doddalahalli Village, Uyyamballi Hobli,
Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
2 Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time the driver of Swift Car bearing No.KA-17-MD-1234 has driven from Doddalahalli towards Sathnoor side i.e.,
from opposite direction, with very high speed, driven extreme its right side, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioners' Motor Cycle, due to which the petitioners' being the rider and pillion rider have sustained grievous injuries and after the accident the petitioner in M.V.C.No.723/2023 was shifted to General hospital, Kanakapura and after first aid he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical,
nourishment, attendant charges etc., and after the accident the petitioner in M.V.C.No.1764/2023 was shifted to General hospital, Kanakapura and after first aid he was shifted to CDSIMER hospital, Harohalli,
wherein admitted as inpatient and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, nourishment,
attendant charges etc.,.
 04.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner in M.V.C.No.723/2023 was hale and healthy, aged about 28 years and was Agriculturist and earning  (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 Rs.30,000/- p.m and prior to the accident, the petitioner in M.V.C.No.1764/2023 was hale and healthy, aged about 30 years and was Agriculturist and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. .
Due to the accidental injuries, both petitioners' cannot attend their work permanently, resulted in loss of earning and put to great financial hardship and untold misery and depressed.

05. The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Swift Car and in this regard the Sathnoor Police have registered a case against the driver of the said offending Swift Car.
The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner of the said offending vehicle and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,

are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/-
respectively to the petitioners together with interest and costs.
06. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels and filed their written statements in both the petitions.

07. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner  (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
3 and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending Car, age, income, occupation of the petitioners and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioners and treatment taken by the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners.

Further he admits that he is the owner of the Swift Car bearing No.KA-17-MD-1234 and it is duly insured with respondent No.2 and the policy is valid and is in force as on the date of accident and the driver had a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and pray for dismiss both the petitions with costs against respondent No.1.
 08.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits issuance of the policy No.DCCR007315399 55/00 and the validity from 19.12.2022 to 18.12.2023 mentioned in the claim petitions in respect of Maruthi Swift Car bearing No.KA-17-MD-1234 and the insurer of the said vehicle and the liability thereof is subject to confirmation of Sec.64VB and the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further denied age,
avocation, income of the petitioners, manner of accident and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioners and treatment taken by the petitioners and  (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 expenses incurred by the petitioners and the compensation claimed is very much excessive,
exorbitant.

In the alleged accident the Maruthi Swift Car bearing No.KA-17-MD-1234 is not involved and it is created and fixed false case against this respondent to get the compensation and there is no rash or negligent act on the part of the driver of the car and the petitioners must have sustained injuries due to their own negligence somewhere else or involvement of some other vehicle, but not involvement of Maruthi Swift Car, the petitioners in collusion with the owner of the car and the Police have filed a false belated complaint against the driver of the admits issuance of policy in respect of Maruthi Swift Car is only to get some compensation.

The driver of the admits issuance of policy in respect of Maruthi Swift Car bearing No.KA-17-MD-1234 was driving the same on the correct side of the road, at that time the claimant/rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-42-Y-4524 along with pillion rider, in a rash and negligent manner, with great speed, without wearing helmet and not having the driving licence and insurance, suddenly came from the opposite directions in the busy road and dashed against the Maruthi Swift Car which was moving on its  (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
4

correct way and the rider also contributed more than 50% negligence, hence the accident is mainly due to negligence of the claimant/rider and hence, pray for dismiss both the petitions with costs against respondent No.2.

09. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
 ISSUES IN MVC NO.723/2023  01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has  sustained grievous injuries in the accident  occurred on 09.01.2023 at about 07.30 p.m, on  Sathanooru Road, near Dodda Alahalli Village,
 Uyyamballi Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk,
 Ramanagara, due to negligent act of driving of  the Swift Car bearing registration No.
 KA-17-MD-1234 by its driver as alleged in the  petition?
 02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?

If so, to what amount and from  whom?
 03. What Order or Award?
 ISSUES IN MVC NO.1764/2023  01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he  has sustained grievous injuries in the accident  (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023  occurred on on 09.01.2023 at about 07.30 p.m,
 on Sathanooru Road, near Dodda Alahalli  Village, Uyyamballi Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk,
 Ramanagara, due to negligent act of driving of  the Swift Car bearing registration No.
 KA-17-MD-1234 by its driver as alleged in the  petition?
 02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?

If so, to what amount and from  whom?
 03.
What Order or Award?

10. The petitioners in both cases in order to prove their case, themselves examined as PW.1 and 2 and got examined doctor in MVC No.723/2023 as PW.3 and they have got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19 and closed their side evidence.

However,
the respondents have not lead their evidence. Hence,
Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
5 respondents evidence is taken as nil.

sentences.text: 11. Both counsels for petitioners and respondents submits their side arguments may be taken as heard.
Hence, petitioners side and respondents side arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.
12. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023  ISSUES IN MVC NO.723/2023
Issue No.1 In the Affirmative
Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative
Issue No.3
As per final order  for the following:-

ISSUES IN MVC NO.1764/2023  Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS  13. Issue No.1 in both cases:- The petitioner in MVC No.723/2023 got himself examined as PW.1 and petitioner in MVC No.1764/2023 got himself examined as PW.2 and they have given evidence in the form of the affidavit and they have reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though, these witnesses have been cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.

14. Further, PW.3 is doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability in MVC  (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 No.723/2023 has stated in his chief-examination evidence that the said petitioner has sustained right femur fracture and he assessed whole body physical disability at 16% and also stated that petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant and estimate of Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
6 this surgery is around Rs.60,000/- and has produced Clinical notes and X-ray as per Ex.P.18 and 19 with respect to petitioner in MVC No.723/2023.
During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that there is no complication in fracture healing and fractures are united and implants are in-situ.

There is no fracture at hip joint and knee joint and admits that petitioner take physiotherapy,
the range of movement and muscle power will be improved and he has assessed present and not functional disability and the present disability may vary.
15 . Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19 on their behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Sathanoor Police, against the driver of offending Car bearing No.KA-17-MD-1234.

Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint given against driver of offending Car for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and  (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 causing grievous injuries to the petitioners.
Ex.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Seizer Mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is copy of IMV report which indicates involvement of both vehicles involved in the alleged accident and front side of both vehicles are damaged.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Wound certificate of the petitioner in MVC No.723/2023 which shows that he sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P.6 is the copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of the offending car for his rash and negligent driving and causing grievous injuries to the petitioners.
Ex.P.8 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending Car.

Ex.P.7 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending Car has admitted that he is the owner of the offending car and driver had a valid driving licence as on the date of accident and said offending car had valid FC and Permit and insurance policy of the offending car is valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Ex.P.10 is copy of the Discharge summary of petitioner in MVC No.723/2023 of Sanjay Gandhi hospital, Bengaluru, which discloses that the petitioner was admitted from 09.01.2023 to  (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 16.01.2023 as inpatient for totally 08 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.11 is Outpatient records of petitioner in MVC No.723/2023.

Ex.P.16 is copy of Wound certificate of the petitioner in MVC Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
7 No.1764/2023 which discloses that said petitioner has sustained three injuries out of them injury Nos.1 and 3 are grievous in nature.

16. On going through the oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioners, it clearly appears that the petitioners have sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 09.01.2023 at about 07.30 p.m, on Sathnoor - Doddalahalli Road, near Solar Plant,
Doddalahalli Village, Uyyamballi Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to rash and negligent driving of Swift Car bearing No.KA-17-MD-1234, by its driver as alleged in the petitions.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative in both cases.
17. Issue No.2 in MVC No.723/2023:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 28 years and was Agriculturist and earning Rs.30,000/-
p.m and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical,
nourishment and attendant charges etc.,.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost income and became permanent disabled.

19. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age,
avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.

However he has produced Ex.P.14 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.15 Driving licence, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 20.07.1994 and the alleged accident was occurred on 09.01.2023 and even these documents are taken into consideration, it appears that as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 29 years and the same is considered for calculating compensation.
As per Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 is 17 and the same is considered.
20. As discussed above, with regard to avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence  (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/-
Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
8 p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-.
 21.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained right femur fracture and he assessed whole body physical disability at 16%.
However, considering the evidence of PW.3 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Ex.P.10 Discharge summary, according to which the petitioner was admitted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital, Bengaluru, as inpatient for 08 days.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge,
 (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore,
considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
under this head.
23. Pain and sufferings:-

As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.3 doctor and Ex.P.11 Outpatient records, Ex.P.18 Clinical notes and Ex.P.19 X-ray and on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
24. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,000/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 08 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 2 months.
Thus, taking into account the notional income  (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/- (Rs.16,000 x 2) under this head.
25. Medical expenses:- As per Ex.P.12 the Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
9 petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.13,740/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.13,740/- under the head of medical expenses.

26. Loss of future amenities in life and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
27. Future medical expenses:-

According to PW.3 doctor the petitioner has sustained right femur fracture and according to him petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant and estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/-
under this head.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount  No. in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 3,26,400-00  2. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00
3 . Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges
4. Medical Expenses 13,740-00  5. Loss of future amenities in 30,000-00  life and unhappiness  6. Loss of income during laid 32,000-00  up period
7 . Future medical expenses 25,000-00  Total 4,87,140-00  29.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner in MVC No.723/2023 is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,87,140/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
 30. Issue No.2 in MVC No.1764/2023:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation  (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
10 on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.
 31.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 30 years and was Agriculturist and earning Rs.30,000/-
p.m and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical,
nourishment and attendant charges etc.,.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost income and became permanent disabled.
32. The said petitioner has not produced any documents with respect to his age, avocation and income and as per Ex.P.16 Wound certificate he sustained grievous injuries.

But he has not examined doctor who treated him and has not produced any Discharge summary and has not produced any Disability certificate and has not produced any Medical bills to prove that he has taken treatment as inpatient in any of the hospital and he has sustained any disability and he has spent any amount towards medical expenses.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his age, avocation and income,
evidence of doctor, Discharge summary, Disability certificate and Medical bills, this tribunal is the
c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.25,000/-.
33 . Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner in MVC No.1764/2023 is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.25,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

34 . Regarding liability:- The respondents have taken several defences, but they have not stepped into witness box and not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners and there is no evidence on record to show that the driver or the owner of the offending vehicle have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further, the respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 4 admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending Car and the same is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.
Further, the respondent No.1 admits that he is the owner of the offending car and it had a valid insurance with respondent No.2.

Hence, respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and  (SCCH-3) 21 M.V.C.No.723/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
11 is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer shall liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.4,87,140/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/-) in MVC No.723/2023 and Global Compensation of Rs.25,000/- in MVC No.
1764/ 2023 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within two months from the date of this Judgment in both cases.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.2 in both cases partly in the affirmative.
35 . Issue No.3 in both cases

: In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2 in both cases,
I proceed to pass the following:-
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner in MVC 723/2023 under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,87,140/- (Rupees Four lakhs eighty seven thousand one hundred and forty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
(SCCH-3) 22 M.V.C.No.723/2023 c/w M.V.C.No.1764/2023 The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner is entitled to get release 75% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 25% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The petition filed by the petitioner in MVC 1764/2023 under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

Since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount with accrued interest shall be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in each case.

Mahesh M vs Prakash H.D on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129049704/
12
Keep the original Judgment and award in MVC No.723/2023 and copy of the same in MVC No.1764/2023.
Draw award accordingly.
